software.name: h17_cpm2202
software.notes: Hard-sectored release, so it boots from the H-88-1 rather than needing the H-37. Disk 1 boots to CONFIGUR; disk 2 carries the BIOS source and the printer utilities.

feature.name: part_id
feature.value: Disk 2 - BIOS source and printer utilities

software.name: h17_cpm2203
software.notes: The H-17 build of 2.2.03, which signs on "FOR H17 DISKS" and reports H/Z17 drives; the soft-sectored H-37 build of the same version is on the h37_flop list. Disk 2 holds the MOVCPM relocators and the printer utilities, disk 3 the BIOS source and MAKEBIOS.

software.name: h17_cpm2204
software.notes: The H-17 build, signing on "FOR H17 DISKS" and dated 09/15/82; the H-37 build of the same version is on the h37_flop list. Disk 2 adds BSYSGEN over 2.2.03 and carries the MOVCPM relocators, disk 3 the BIOS source. The setup disk boots on its own into the Zenith Setup 2.0 front end. These are the h17disk version 2 images from Mark Garlanger's library, read on an Applesauce, so they carry the sector headers and the per-sector read status as well as the data.

software.name: h17_hdos_500000
software.notes: Issue 50.00.00, the original release. It predates the H-89 and H-88, whose 8250 console is only driven from issue 50.03.00 on, so it runs on the H8 alone. Both issues ship in the same archive upstream. Its disk initializer is INIT17, not INIT: it verifies the media by timing the sector holes in CPU loop iterations, a window calibrated for the H8's 8080, which is why the 50.03.00 build of it fails on the Z80 machines (see that entry). HDOS 1.5 replaced INIT17 with INIT and dropped the check.

software.name: h17_hdos_500300
software.notes: Issue 50.03.00, the first HDOS release to support the H-89 and H-88, adding the 8250 console used on those machines. The earlier issue 50.00.00, which runs on the H8 alone, is a separate entry on this list. Its disk initializer INIT17 does not work on the H-88 or H-89: before writing anything it checks the media by counting CPU loop iterations per sector-hole period, against a window calibrated for the H8's 8080, and the Z80 runs the same loop at a different rate (31 T-states per pass against the 8080's 29 at the same 2.048 MHz), so every disk is rejected with WRONG TYPE OF MEDIA. It boots and runs on those machines otherwise. To initialize disks there use the INIT from HDOS 1.5 (issue 50.04.00) or later, which dropped the check; INIT17 itself works on the H8.

software.name: h17_hdos_500600
software.notes: Shipped as three separately numbered disks, all bootable: the system itself (890-64), Software Tools (890-103) and Driver Source (890-104). These are the h17disk version 2 images from Mark Garlanger's library. They hold the same sector data as the SEBHC .h8d set, and add the sector headers and the per-sector read status.

software.name: h17_hugdisk2
software.notes: This is a non-bootable HDOS 1.5 disk. Boot HDOS from another disk, then put this disk in a second drive. The disk holds two machine code games, Space War and Life, and five Benton Harbor BASIC games: Death Star, Market, Camel, Football and Qubic. README.DOC describes each game and names its author. Football uses the H8 front panel keypad and LEDs, so it runs only on the H8. The files are dated 31-Mar-80.

info.name: usage
info.value: To run a machine code game, type SPACEWAR or LIFE at the HDOS prompt. To run a BASIC game, start BASIC, type OLD"name", then type RUN. MARKINST holds the instructions for Market, so load and run it before MARKET.
